text:
Jaroslav Chmelar is a fifth-round pick from 2021 playing eight and a half minutes a night on the Rangers' fourth line, and he's made a few of them count. His breakaway shorthanded goal against Devon Levi in Edmonton was the highlight, two nights after he scored in Seattle, and Forever Blueshirts described him as being on a mission. Yahoo Sports wrote he's making the most of his chance.

He's played 13 games with two goals and an assist, and the finishing is fair, 2 goals on 1.35 expected. The bigger numbers are less kind: the Rangers take 42% of the five-on-five expected goals (the quality of chances) with him on, about 12 points worse than without him. That's common for fourth-liners in small samples, and the team has scored a little more than expected during his shifts.

He hits (23 in 13 games) and our model's closest comparison is Trent Frederic, a big depth forward who finishes more than he passes. His AHL season in Hartford translated to about 16 points over 82 NHL games. Our talent range has him around 9 goals if he stays in the lineup. For a fourth-line spot, the goals are a strong argument.
